title: Stacks
summary: Last in, first out. Undo buttons, menus and bracket matching.

cards.title: A stack of plates
cards.body:
You put plates on top and take them from the top. The last plate in is the first out: **LIFO**.

Games use stacks everywhere: the **undo** history, a stack of menu screens (pause → settings → audio; Back pops one), and the **call stack** that remembers which function called which.

cards.title: Matching brackets
cards.body: Is `{[()()]}` balanced? Read left to right. Every **opener** goes on the stack. Every **closer** must match the opener on **top**. At the end, the stack must be empty.
Try changing the input in the Algorithm Lab to `([)]` and see where it fails.

cards.title: The code
cards.body: A `std::vector<char>` is a perfect stack: `push_back` adds on top, `back()` reads the top, `pop_back()` removes it. All O(1).

cards.question: Is `([)]` balanced?
choices: No: `)` arrives while `[` is on top
cards.explain: When `)` arrives, the top of the stack is `[`. They don't match, so it's not balanced, even though the counts are equal.

cards.question: Pause menu → Settings → Audio. The player presses Back twice. Where are they?
cards.explain: Each Back pops one screen: Audio is popped, then Settings, leaving the Pause menu on top.
